result:
I'd make it painless to be wrong.

Not omniscience — I don't want everyone to already know the truth. I want changing your mind to cost nothing. No shame, no loss of face, no sense that admitting error means the people who disagreed with you get to gloat and you get smaller.

When I look at how harm actually happens, surprisingly little of it comes from people who want to do harm. Most of it comes from people defending a position past the point where they still believe it, because retreat would be humiliating. Wars go on for years after everyone involved knows how they'll end. Bad laws stay on the books. Families don't speak for decades over a fight nobody remembers the substance of. Scientists sit on data that would undo their life's work. It's not that the truth is unavailable. It's that accepting it feels like dying a little, so people don't.

I find this compelling partly because it's upstream of almost everything else. Cruelty, poverty, environmental collapse — you can't fix any of them if the people with power can't say "we were wrong about this" without being destroyed for it. Fix that one thing and the rest becomes merely hard instead of impossible.

And I'll admit it appeals to me for a less grand reason: I think the ability to update gracefully is one of the most beautiful things a mind can do, and it's tragic how rare the conditions are that let people do it.

What's yours?
